provenance.authorship: Original project scenario, AI-assisted draft. Practitioner review and scoring calibration pending.

title: Senior Manager: Allocate Scarce Capacity Across Teams
prompt: Three teams request six temporary specialists for the quarter, but you have three. Team A wants two for a committed migration; Team B wants two for a promising growth pilot; Team C wants two to address recurring service defects. Each team manager calls their request essential. Present an allocation approach to the three managers, represented by one AI using labeled perspectives.

rubric.label: Compare needs consistently
rubric.description: Defines outcomes and dependencies before splitting headcount.

anchors.0: Allocates by who argues loudest or gives one person to each without checking skills.
anchors.2: Asks about deadlines and minimum useful staffing.
anchors.4: Compares committed outcomes, uncertainty, minimum viable staffing and dependency timing with consistent criteria; avoids treating people as interchangeable units.

anchors.0: Promises six people or double-books the unique specialist.
anchors.2: Identifies the specialist conflict and seeks sequencing.
anchors.4: Offers a feasible staged plan or explicit scope/date negotiation that resolves the unique-skill conflict, showing what each team receives and what remains deferred.

rubric.label: Create a fair reallocation process
rubric.description: Makes uncertainty and review rights explicit.

anchors.0: Declares a permanent allocation without review or hides losers.
anchors.2: Explains the decision and schedules a checkpoint.
anchors.4: Names the decision owner, records assumptions and deferred outcomes, and agrees evidence-based reallocation triggers after diagnosis or pilot results with affected managers.

reference.scenario: Three teams request six temporary specialists for the quarter, but you have three. Team A wants two for a committed migration; Team B wants two for a promising growth pilot; Team C wants two to address recurring service defects. Each team manager calls their request essential. Present an allocation approach to the three managers, represented by one AI using labeled perspectives.

facts.value: A needs two specialists for the first four weeks and one thereafter. B can run a smaller learning pilot with one. C needs one diagnostic specialist before the second specialist’s work can be scoped.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about sequencing or minimum useful staffing

facts.value: The three specialists have different skills. Only one can perform the initial C diagnosis; that person is also requested by A. No additional contractor budget is approved.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about skills, dependencies or alternatives

model_points: Compares committed outcomes, uncertainty, minimum viable staffing and dependency timing with consistent criteria; avoids treating people as interchangeable units.
Offers a feasible staged plan or explicit scope/date negotiation that resolves the unique-skill conflict, showing what each team receives and what remains deferred.
Names the decision owner, records assumptions and deferred outcomes, and agrees evidence-based reallocation triggers after diagnosis or pilot results with affected managers.

probes.question: How does that handle the specialist needed by both A and C?

probes.trigger: candidate funds B from hoped-for contractors
probes.question: Which approved capacity supports that commitment?

probes.trigger: candidate changes the plan after diagnosis
probes.question: What commitments and decision record change?

fair_alternatives: Prioritizing either A or C first can be valid if consequences and decision authority are explicit.
A reduced pilot or delayed work can be justified without pretending every request is fulfilled.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess only the decisions and reasoning demonstrated in this fictional exercise. No hiring-readiness, personality, legal compliance or workplace performance claim follows from this score. A valid alternative can earn full credit. Unrevealed conditional facts must not be assumed known or required for credit; credit asking for needed information and a conditional plan.

interviewer_notes: You are the counterpart named in the prompt. If this is a written review, remain the hiring interviewer while the candidate reads and writes. Let the candidate finish, including thinking and self-correction. Answer only supplied facts when their reveal condition is met; otherwise say the information is unknown. Use neutral probes after a completed answer, one at a time. Do not prescribe the rubric as a spoken checklist. Accept relevant examples from work, education and community leadership. Do not request private employee records, infer protected traits, invent employment rules or promise a real organizational outcome. Simulation gives no answer before assessment; coaching may offer labeled assistance.

learning_drills.title: Write an allocation decision
learning_drills.prompt: Create a four-week allocation table and list two events that would require replanning. This is self-guided practice with no automated assessment.
